title: The Maize Reference Genome: Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0
description: The Maize reference genome (Zea mays, assembly Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0) spans approximately 2.18 Gb across 10 chromosomes, encoding approx 39,700 protein-coding genes (estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
key_points: Assembly Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0: the public reference coordinates.
standards: Coordinates follow the named assembly Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0
